enonce_intro_markdown:
![fig-1](gce-ol-maths-2020-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_11_fig_1.png)

In Figure 3, $APQ$ is a circum-circle. The chord $AP$ subtends an angle of $120^\circ$ at the centre, $O$, of the circle. Calculate the values of the angles:

figures.legende: Figure 3 : cercle de centre O avec les points A, P, Q ; angle AOP = 120 degres, x = angle OAP, y = angle AQP.

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the value of the angle $x$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
$O$ is the centre, so $OA = OP$ (radii): triangle $OAP$ is isosceles, and its base angles are equal. $x$ is the angle $OAP$ and the angle at the centre is $\angle AOP = 120^\circ$.

$x = \dfrac{180^\circ - 120^\circ}{2} = \dfrac{60^\circ}{2} = 30^\circ$.

**Answer: $x = 30^\circ$.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the value of the angle $y$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
$y$ is the angle $AQP$ at the circumference, subtended by the chord $AP$, whose angle at the centre is $\angle AOP = 120^\circ$.

The angle at the centre is **twice** the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc: $y = \dfrac{120^\circ}{2} = 60^\circ$.

**Answer: $y = 60^\circ$.**
